summary:
Fireline is an SI-powered workspace that turns NASA's PSI microgravity combustion archive into a structured knowledge base for fire-safety research. Users create research sessions on an interactive graph canvas, attach mission documents and data sources, and work with an embedded AI agent (or one connected via MCP) that searches the indexed knowledge, assembles evidence on the canvas, and links every claim to its source. 

The system indexes and labels data — materials, fuels, hardware, environments, incidents — adding a layer of relations between documents so users can compare investigations, spot research gaps, and build well-informed conclusions before committing to a mission.

The current prototype is a working mock focused on one end-to-end use case: a lunar rover cabin material review built entirely from real PSI data. It demonstrates the full intended workflow — search, graph reasoning, evidence coverage maps, and gap registers — and shows how the platform would scale to any domain: the ingestion pipeline normalizes heterogeneous scientific data (tables, reports, metadata) into a unified knowledge graph and can be extended with new sources and investigations as they become available.
details:
Fireline is a generalized knowledge-base interface for scientific research, built around a simple principle: an AI can only produce trustworthy conclusions when the context it works from is structured, indexed, and traceable. The workspace presents four linked views:

1. Analyze

A three-pane session workspace:

- copilot chat on the left,

- Neo4j-style graph canvas in the center,

- a details/summary panel on the right.

Users define a research question, attach mission documents and data sources, and the agent finds the most relevant evidence, adds investigation and dataset nodes to the canvas, and preserves engineer-provided assumptions, measured data, and unknowns as visually distinct node types.

2. Explore

A search engine over the indexed knowledge with facet filters (safety area, context, file type) and results grouped into data, investigations, and source documents, with a working set for selecting files.

3. Visualize

Chart templates (scatter, line, bar, coverage maps) over chosen datasets with axis mapping, handed off from the Explore view.

4. Flame VR

A 3D model simulation of a potential fire in the analyzed environment.

The data pipeline

The core of the system is an ingestion pipeline that normalizes heterogeneous scientific data into a unified knowledge graph.

It takes whatever a source provides — messy experimental tables with mixed units and conventions, free-text metadata, catalog records, report archives — and turns it into typed, queryable entities: investigations, datasets, materials, fuels, hardware, platforms, environments, and incidents, connected by labeled relations (a study uses a hardware, targets an environment, produced a dataset).

The pipeline auto-detects unit conventions, repairs common transcription artifacts, and flags anything it cannot verify rather than silently correcting it. Every investigation receives a transparent relevance score with explicit, human-readable reasons — a retrieval ranking, never a fire probability. In the full product, this pipeline is the growth mechanism: as new PSI investigations land, or entirely new sources are connected (external databases, standards libraries, mission documents via MCP), the same ingestion normalizes and indexes them into the existing graph, so the knowledge base expands without re-engineering.

AI-assisted research

The copilot operates over the indexed graph rather than raw text, so it answers questions with actual numbers and citations. It searches the knowledge base, assembles the best-matching evidence onto the canvas in ranked groups (direct match, screening context, atmosphere context, separate follow-up branches), and attaches clickable references to the source record. In the intended full form, the same agent layer is available through an MCP connector so external tools can operate on the same indexed context.

Visualization

Beyond the chart templates, the workspace includes an immersive WebXR viewer (Three.js) that reconstructs raw archival camera data of a cool-flame experiment into volumetric emission fields, alongside a reduced physics model computed in a browser worker.

Users can grab, rotate, and resize the flame and sensor panels with hand tracking, and switch between measured reconstruction and model — with every assumption explicitly marked as estimated or inferred.

Current state.

The prototype is a fully functional mock: the frontend, data pipeline, graph, and agent are all real, but the agent is a deterministic intent router over the indexed data rather than a live LLM, and the external document connectors are simulated with seeded fixtures.

The demo is deliberately scoped to one end-to-end use case — a fire-safety engineer reviewing cabin materials for a pressurized lunar rover at 30% oxygen and one-sixth gravity — chosen because it exposes the platform's hardest design problem: comparing mission-specific conditions against experimental evidence. The agent surfaces the closest PSI evidence (Saffire-II material samples), preserves the original test conditions, and produces an auditable gap register showing that no solid-material test has ever covered the rover's atmosphere — the exact input a mission review board needs to justify the next test campaign.

Tech stack:

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind v4 + shadcn-style UI, a graph canvas library, Recharts for chart templates, Zustand for persistent state, Three.js/WebXR for VR, and a Node.js/TypeScript pipeline for data ingestion and processing, with Python for scientific reconstruction.

Repository: https://github.com/Sepy-NASA/Fireline/tree/main

Why it matters

The challenge is to make 13.5 TB of PSI data findable, comparable, and interpretable. Fireline turns "the data can be overwhelming" into a defensible, auditable statement of what is covered and what is not — and the generalized platform is designed to do the same for any scientific domain, as NASA's data archive grows.
